AM RECEIVER BASICSE
AM receivers are electronic devices that pick up signals sent from AM transmitters.
DISCUSSION
DEFINITION
RECEIVER - A receiver is any electronic device that converts radio waves into audio, video or any form that is useful.
DEFINITION
TRANSMITTER - A transmitter is any electronic device that converts intelligence into radio waves. Intelligence can be audio, video, data or any useful form of information.
The AM broadcast band covers frequencies from 500 kHz to 1600 kHz.
The abbreviation AM stands for Amplitude Modulation.
AM is one form of modulation that is used to transmit intelligence over long distances.
Intelligence is the information transferred from one location to another.
In the AM band, the intelligence can be voice, music, data or video.
The intelligence to be transmitted is a relatively low frequency, usually 15 kHz or less.
These low frequencies are not well suited for long distance transmissions.
These low frequencies are not well suited for long distance transmissions.

TRANSMISSION OF WAVES - Low frequencies tend to follow the curvature of the earth and are easily blocked by buildings and absorbed by the landscape. High frequencies tend to bounce off the atmosphere making long distance communication possible.
The AM broadcast band uses higher frequencies, called carrier signals to transmit the intelligence.
High frequencies are capable of being transmitted over hundreds of miles.
High frequencies are capable of being transmitted over hundreds of miles.
Transmitters use carrier frequencies to "carry" the intelligence through the atmosphere.
Amplitude modulation occurs when the carrier frequency is altered in amplitude by the lower intelligence frequency.
The low frequency intelligence rides on the high frequency carrier.
This allows the intelligence to be transmitted long distances.
The modulated signal is then transmitted as an electromagnetic wave.
The modulated signal is then transmitted as an electromagnetic wave.
ELECTROMAGNETIC WAVE - Any class of waves transmitted by a system of electric and magnetic fields.
To operate, a receiver must perform the functions of reception, selection, detection and reproduction.
Reception is the action of transmitted electromagnetic waves passing through the receiver's antenna.
The electromagnetic wave induces a voltage in the antenna that is then processed by the receiver.
Induced voltage in the antenna is very weak, usually less than 100 micro volts.
Selection is the ability of the receiver to isolate one station's frequency from the many present at the antenna.
Detection is the action of separating the low frequency intelligence from the high frequency carrier.
Reproduction is the action of converting detected intelligence into sound waves that a human can hear.

DISCUSSION
The detector recovers the original audio from the IF signal.
The audio frequency amplifier (AF amplifier) increases the detected audio enough to drive the speaker.
The RF and local oscillator frequencies are combined in the mixer.
The mixer produces four frequencies, the RF, LO, sum and difference frequencies..
With a received RF frequency of 1100 kHz the four mixer frequencies are1100 kHz, 1555 kHz, 2655 kHz and 455 kHz.
The difference frequency is also called the intermediate frequency (IF).
The LO frequency minus the RF frequency equals the IF.
DEFINITION
INTERMEDIATE FREQUENCY (IF) - The intermediate frequency is a standard frequency that receivers convert all incoming signals to.
The local oscillator provides a frequency to mix with the selected RF signal.

The next function on the block diagram is the Intermediate Frequency Amplifier.
The difference frequency (455 kHz) from the tuner is amplified by the IF amplifier stages to a usable level.
The IF amplifiers also filter out any other frequencies that may be passed from the tuner.
The amplified signal is sent to the detector next..........
Detection is the process of recovering the original modulation signal from the IF signal.
The detector is normally a diode that is used in conjunction with a series of low pass filters.
The rectifier diode eliminates the positive or the negative audio signal from the carrier.
The RC circuit removes the high frequency 455 kHz from the low frequency audio.
The action of the detector blocks the carrier and passes audio to the AF amplifier.
The final block in the basic AM receiver is the audio amplifier.
The audio amplifier receives the signal from the detector and amplifies it to a usable level that can drive a speaker.
The AF amplifier consists of a pre-amplifier, a driver and a push-pull amplifier.
The pre-amplifier amplifies the DC level of the incoming signal.
The pre-amplifier amplifies the DC level of the incoming signal.
The driver amplifies the audio signals' current to a level that drives the push-pull amplifier.
The push-pull amplifier increases power to a level that will drive the speaker.
